title: A report from a format template

blocks.text: The page's best practice fills a report with a text block template, and its edge cases add the catch: when `formatted()` or `String.format` reads a template, a `%` that should be printed is written **`%%`**. The page's example report is:
Write `Report.summary(String quarter, long revenue, Integer growth)`. It returns the lines above joined by `\n`, with no newline at the end:

items: `Revenue: $<revenue>`, with a comma between every three digits;

blocks.text: The output must not depend on where the program runs: `formatted()` uses the JVM's default locale, which may group digits with `.` or a space. Format with `String.format(Locale.ROOT, ...)` instead, for every line, the growth line included (some locales even write digits in another script).

cases.says: The quarter and the revenue, grouped by thousands, fill the report's lines; with no growth there is no growth line.
The growth line ends with a literal %, written %% in the template.
The thousands separator is a comma whatever the JVM's default locale is.

concepts: A template formatted with an explicit Locale.ROOT does not depend on the JVM's default locale for digit grouping.
A literal % in a formatted() or String.format template is written %%.
